exam.subject: Chemistry
exam.title: ESSCE-style Chemistry 2nd Semester Model Exam 2010/11

parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: PART-I Contains 75 multiple-choice questions. You must answer all of them. Each question carries 1 point. Write all the answers on the SCANTRON ANSWER SHEETS. There is only one best answer for each question. Blacken the letter of your choice on the ANSWER SHEET with a pencil.

parts.title: Part II – Workout and Short Answer Questions
parts.instructions: This part contains 5 questions. You must answer all of them. Each question carries 5 points. A total of 25 points. Write your answers on separate answer sheet provided.

questions.stem: Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) is a blood sugar which breaks down in human tissues to release energy. This process is called aerobic respiration, requires oxygen. The reaction is C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy.  i. Calculate the percentage mass of oxygen in glucose.  ii. How many liters of oxygen is required completely to burn 0.5 mole of glucose at STP?
questions.answer: i. 53.3% oxygen in glucose.  ii. 67.2 L O₂ at STP.
accepted_answers: i. 53.3% oxygen in glucose.  ii. 67.2 L O₂ at STP.
explanation_steps: Given: C₆H₁₂O₆ M=180; reaction uses 6 mol O₂ per 1 mol glucose
ii. 0.5 mol glucose needs 3.0 mol O₂; at STP 3×22.4 = 67.2 L
questions.marking_points: 2 for %O working; 3 for O₂ volume (1 for mole ratio 1:6, 1 for 3 mol, 1 for 67.2 L).
tips: % element = (atoms × Ar / Mr) × 100. STP molar volume = 22.4 L mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: A. Draw the structure of each of the following hydrocarbons. i. 4-ethylhex-2-ene  ii. 3,3,5-Trimethyl-1-octyne. B. Complete the following reaction i. H₂SO₄ + NaOH  ii. CH₃─C≡CH + 2H₂
questions.answer: A.i. C6 chain, C=C between C2–C3, ethyl on C4: CH₃CH=CHCH(C₂H₅)CH₂CH₃. A.ii. C8 chain, C≡C at C1, two methyls on C3 and one on C5. B.i. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. B.ii. CH₃C≡CH + 2H₂ → CH₃CH₂CH₃ (Ni/Pt).
accepted_answers: A.i. C6 chain, C=C between C2–C3, ethyl on C4: CH₃CH=CHCH(C₂H₅)CH₂CH₃. A.ii. C8 chain, C≡C at C1, two methyls on C3 and one on C5. B.i. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. B.ii. CH₃C≡CH + 2H₂ → CH₃CH₂CH₃ (Ni/Pt).
explanation_steps: Given: two IUPAC names and two reactions
Longest chain first, number from the multiple bond
Acid + base → salt + water; alkyne + 2H₂ → alkane
questions.marking_points: 1.5 each correct skeletal structure; 1 for complete neutralisation; 1 for propane / fully hydrogenated product.
tips: -ene number from the end nearer the double bond. -yne at C1 already fixes the numbering.

questions.stem: When a mixture of methane gas and steam is passed over a heated nickel catalyst at high temperature, water gas is formed. How many grams of methane are required to produce 11.2 g of carbon monoxide? (At.mass: H=1, C=12, O=16)
explanation_steps: Given: steam reforming CH₄ + H₂O → CO + 3H₂ (water gas) and 11.2 g CO
n(CO)=11.2/28=0.40 mol; mole ratio CH₄:CO = 1:1 so n(CH₄)=0.40 mol
m(CH₄)=0.40×16=6.4 g if the equation is CH₄+H₂O→CO+3H₂

Some texts write 2CH₄ + O₂ / other oxidants; with steam reforming the 1:1 ratio gives 6.4 g. 11.2 g is 0.4 mol CO; if they expected 8 g they used Mr(CH₄)=16 and 0.5 mol (half of 22.4 g CO). Recheck: 11.2 g CO = 0.4 mol → 6.4 g CH₄.
questions.marking_points: 1 for equation; 1 for n(CO)=0.4 mol; 1 for 1:1 ratio; 2 for 6.4 g.
tips: Write the equation first. Water-gas / steam reforming is 1 mol CH₄ per 1 mol CO.
